audit.whatIsWrong: Petrifying Gaze is named in four places and described every time as a cone that simply 'stuns you mid-dive'. The facing condition — the entire counterplay — appears nowhere.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Cassiopeia releases a swirl of magical energy from her eyes, stunning any enemies in front of her that are facing her and slowing any others with their back turned.' Turning away downgrades a 120s stun into a slow. For a melee champion whose whole plan is to arrive on top of her, that is the difference between dying in the dive and walking out of it.
audit.corrected: phases[4].why, breakdown.cooldowns, report[5].t and whys[6] now state that it only stuns enemies facing her.

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer calls Cassiopeia 'he' and 'his' from the tldr down — 'He kites you out', 'his Miasma', 'His early', 'His answer goes first', 'if he snowballs'. Level 2's 'why' also claimed 'dash-resets stack your passive shield mid-trade'.
audit.why: Drakehound's Step grants bonus attack range, damage, attack speed and an energy refund — no shield anywhere; Repudiation is Ambessa's only shield. And the stage that decides the early lane is not a shield, it is Miasma's 24s cooldown at rank 1: that is the longest cooldown on Cassiopeia's bar and the only window in which Ambessa's dash survives contact.
audit.corrected: tldr, enemyWin, report[0].t and phases[1].why rewritten with the right pronoun and the 24s number.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level 6's 'why' was the generic 'the R lock isolates and finishes the chain — point it at the kill, not the tank', with no mention of Petrifying Gaze's timer.
audit.why: Petrifying Gaze is 120s at rank 1 against Public Execution's 130s — she gets her ultimate back faster than Ambessa does, so a traded pair of ults is a losing exchange for Ambessa unless the dive actually kills.
audit.corrected: phases[4].why now carries both ultimate cooldowns and the facing rule.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns named Miasma's effect but gave no number, and never mentioned that Noxious Blast and Twin Fang are effectively always available.
audit.why: Miasma runs 24s at rank 1 down to 16s; Noxious Blast is 3.5s and Twin Fang 0.75s. That is the real shape of the lane — two abilities she can spam and one long cooldown that is the only thing standing between Ambessa and a gap-close.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d and report[5].t now carry the real numbers.

audit.whatIsWrong: No anti-heal anywhere in the matchup, and the item line ends at Mercury's Treads.
audit.why: Riot's Twin Fang text: it 'deals increased damage to Poisoned targets and heals her for a percentage of the damage dealt', on a 0.75s cooldown. Against a target sitting in Miasma that is continuous healing off the same damage that is killing you, so Grievous Wounds is what makes any extended trade payable.
audit.corrected: report[8].t now adds Oblivion Orb against Twin Fang.

edits.after: She kites you out — survive it, then commit inside the 24s gap after Miasma. Petrifying Gaze only stuns you if you face her.

notes: Cassiopeia is written as 'he' throughout the templated half of the full layer; I fixed the tldr and report[0], and the remaining copies sit in breakdown.wave, breakdown.mid, breakdown.feeding, breakdown.late, report[1], report[2], report[4], report[9] and report[12], all of which are duplicate boilerplate sentences. The content layer twice calls Serpentine Grace her 'no-boots passive' — Riot's description only says 'All Move Speed bonuses are more effective on Cassiopeia', with nothing about boots, so I left those strings untouched rather than assert or delete a claim the data cannot settle. Ambessa's kit file flags grounding on Repudiation and on Public Execution plus healing on R; Riot's descriptions contain none of that, so I never suggested she can ground Cassiopeia back or heal off her ultimate.
